implementation_summary: Added marketing-signals.ts, which exports marketingSignals, auditMarketing, isLeadForm, ON_PAGE_SEO_RULES and TAG_TOOLS. It always returns ten entries, one per MARKETING_SIGNALS key, in that order and with each key's label. Every entry is 'found' or 'not-found'. 'not-checked' is used only when no page was read. Details use fixed wording, and page lists stop after 5 pages with 'and N more'. How each signal is decided: on-page SEO counts pages with a title, a meta description or an H1 and cites SEO findings on read pages. Schema lists the JSON-LD types found. Internal linking reports the pages with internal links, how many pages are reached (from inboundCounts) and the unlinkedPages. Social tags reports og: and twitter: separately. Analytics matches known tag hosts by exact host or subdomain. CTAs uses PageContent.ctas. Lead forms ignores hidden, submit and button fields, rejects forms with a password field and search forms, and otherwise needs an email or tel field or a name/email/phone word in the field's name or label. Click-to-call counts tel: contact links plus tel: anchors not already listed. Trust signals come from Review, AggregateRating or Rating JSON-LD, review widget hosts, and review, testimonial or certification text. Local signals combines NAP, map embeds and LocalBusiness schema and fills `nap`. Added nap.ts, which reads NAP from LocalBusiness JSON-LD (including @graph and subtypes, turning PostalAddress into one line) and from <address> text. In address text the first line is the name and the remaining lines are the address; the phone comes from a phone-only line or a labelled phone, else from the page's first tel: link. Each value is capped at 200 characters, a page keeps at most 5 NAP entries, and duplicates are dropped. Both modules are pure: they make no requests, submit nothing and do not change their input.

risks: On-page SEO cites findings by rule name (missing-title, missing-description, duplicate-title, duplicate-description, no-h1, multiple-h1, skipped-heading-level), taken from the BE-305/content-problems acceptance criteria in tasks.json. If that task emits different rule keys, update ON_PAGE_SEO_RULES.
Trust and lead-form detection uses English heuristics, so Tamil pages may come out as 'not-found' for trust signals.
In an <address> element, NAP treats the first of two or more lines as the business name. An address element without a name line would put the street in name.
The 'certification' text match is deliberately narrow and can miss some pages.
NAP values are copied as the page shows them, capped at 200 characters. A page could show a person's phone in an <address> element.
handoff: analyse-site should call marketingSignals({ pages: recorded.map(p => ({ raw: p.raw, content: p.content })), internalLinking, findings }) after the content findings have AF-NNN ids, then call auditMarketing(readPaths, signals). Pages are de-duplicated by content.urlPath, keeping the first. isLocalBusinessType and napFromPage in nap.ts can be reused. The barrel should export marketingSignals and auditMarketing. Detail strings contain no ADR 0018 claim words; in particular 'certified' is avoided and 'certifications' is used instead.
